assets.name: Kaspa

score_rationales.institutional: Kaspa has early-stage institutional infrastructure — Zodia Custody (Standard Chartered subsidiary) supports KAS, Valour has launched a KAS ETP in Europe, and Marathon Digital mines it — but there is no US ETF, no major corporate treasury adoption, no Grayscale product, and the dedicated treasury vehicle (Krescendo Capital) is seed-stage and niche; overall footprint remains thin relative to its market cap.
score_rationales.regulatory: Kaspa's PoW consensus gives it a Bitcoin-adjacent commodity profile — the strongest regulatory posture an altcoin can hold — and it has no adverse enforcement actions, Zodia Custody (Standard Chartered) institutional-grade custody, and live Valor Finance ETPs in Europe under MiCA. However, KAS has no explicit US commodity designation from the CFTC, no SEC-registered ETF filing, and insufficient market footprint to attract formal regulatory attention (positive or negative), leaving its US classification unsettled and any ETF pathway still speculative.
score_rationales.supply: KAS has a hard cap of 28.70B with 95.57% already circulating (27.42B of 27.43B total supply out), leaving only ~1.27B (~4.4%) yet to be mined under a monthly halving schedule that makes future emission negligible and front-loaded dilution effectively over. The fair-launch PoW origin (no pre-mine, no VC allocation, no team unlock cliffs) eliminates structured sell-side overhangs entirely, which is the strongest single tokenomics signal. Score is capped below 85 because no concrete exchange-reserve trend data or on-chain long-term holder ratio was supplied, preventing verification of whether the near-complete supply is accumulating off-exchange or sitting in liquid sell-ready wallets.
